"I think perhaps I was a bird in another life," he said softly as he stroked the delicate feather clasped between his fingers. "I dream of flying every night."

"Daniel, wake up!" screamed Muriel. "We are going to die here!"

The dull thuds of explosions all around the city were heard and felt by both of them. Gunfire from the floors below continued to get closer by the minute. She couldn't help but wonder why he had postponed leaving for so long. Now, it was too late.

"We are leaving, my love," he said calmly. "Very soon now."

"There is no way out! The enemy has entered the city! They are in the building! Do you not hear it? Are you even paying attention to anything beyond your constant tinkering?" She was crying openly.

He held her close for a moment to comfort her. She was right, they should have left sooner. He grabbed his pack from the chair and strapped it on. He then went to the balcony doors and threw them open. Light flooded the room. He turned to her, holding out his hand.

"Come to me."

"What are you doing, Daniel?" she cried.

"You must trust me," he replied. "Hurry now."

She walked to him and took his hand. He guided her to the very edge of the balcony and helped her to the rail. They stood there together, balanced on the edge for a moment. She felt this was a fitting end. Better to die hurling towards earth until her final embrace ended them than wait here for the enemy. She was ready to die. She felt his arms encircling her and closed her eyes.

"No matter what happens next, remember that I love you," he whispered in her ear. She heard a series of metallic clicks. She realized she was now strapped to Daniel.

"What...?" she began.

"Now!" he cried as he propelled them forward.

Daniel pushed her head down, pulling her behind him as he took off running.

Their feet pounded in an eerie rhythm. He could feel his blood thrumming through his veins. He would damn this whole backward world, if not for her.

Muriel gazed after him, terror and awe mingled on her near-perfect features. He pulled her into a narrow side street -more of an alley, really- and tugged her body against his.

"Daniel, what..." she began.

"Hush."

He registered the momentary pain in her eyes, and held a finger to her lips. The sounds of booted feet grew nearer, and she nodded her understanding. Shadows filled the street entrance; paused. Passed.

He let his hand fall to his side. Muriel's breathing was heavy, ragged. Her chest heaved as she stared up at him.

She will never believe me, he thought. She would think him mad, run from him in disgust. Or worse. What if she believed him and rejected him for the truth?

He took a deep, calming breath. It didn't work. Nerves got the better of him, and he found himself unable to speak for a moment.

Her hand pressed against his chest, slid up to curl around his shoulder. "Is tech-no-logy magic?"

"The thing is, Muriel," he began, "This isn't really my world."

Her lips twisted; her delicate eyebrows furrowed in confusion. "Your world?"

He couldn't do it. She trusted him, he knew. He couldn't bear to see that trust fade, when she realized he hadn't been honest with her.

Her head tilted back, eyes seeking his. Her lips were slightly parted. Ripe. Full. His head lowered to hers.

A shadow fell over them.

"I found one!"

Daniel shoved Muriel to the ground just as the shadow fired.

Daniel raised Muriel to her feet and took her hand. The sound of raised voices and heavy boots on the cobblestones were getting close now.

"Come, my love," he implored.

She hesitated, only for an instant, but it was there. The doubt and indecision shown her eyes. Should she go with him? She was only going to bring trouble to him now, something that would not be true if she had never used her powers.

He sensed her doubt. His eyes questioned, but there was no more time for words. He squeezed her hand and pulled gently for her to follow.

Doubt gave way to devotion, she was trapped. She had no choice but to to follow the man she loved. Maybe later she would find the strength to leave him, but that moment was not now.

They dodged market vendors and their stalls, the throng of people making it difficult to move as quickly as they so desperately needed to. As they finally cleared the market square, shouts were raised far behind them. The soldiers had reached the square. Daniel veered them towards a narrow alleyway. Shattered brick pelted his face as a bullet struck the wall near his head. He cried out in pain, but kept running.

The alley was uncomfortably constricting. He immediately wished he had chosen a different course. There was no choice now but to push on.

A door opened ahead of them, a wizened old man stood holding it open, blocking the way forward. He appeared to be a man of very simple means. He is clothes were threadbare and worn. In his hand, he held a smoking pipe. Daniel caught the scent of the tobacco. It reminded him of home.

"Quickly children," said the man. "Come this way."

He seemed so calm. As if he had been expecting them. Daniel trusted him immediately. He somehow knew that this man was a friend.

They ducked inside and found themselves in a dimly lit room. A fire burned in the hearth, giving off the only light. Daniel tried to make out the various items that surrounded them on high shelves, but could not quite make out any details.

The old man lead them to chairs set before the fire. As they sat, he stoked the fire, adding another log. Finally, he sighed and took a chair himself.

"Oh my," he said quietly. "You two are in a bit of a spot."

Muriel gazed warily around the room. Too many shadows. The old man could be concealing anything in here. Her instinct was to trust him, but she'd been fooled before.

She reached instinctively for Daniel's hand, and found it already seeking her own. The fire cast the old man's shadow across their intertwined fingers like a seal as he moved to his seat.

"Oh my," he said quietly. "You two are in a bit of a spot."

Muriel choked back a laugh. That was an understatement. Not that he would know that. He only saw two people, running from something in a world where everyone was always on the run. He probably did this every day.

Unless her instincts were wrong. Maybe his motives were more sinister. Blackmail? A bounty? Murder? She leaned forward in her chair, ready to interrogate him, but Daniel cut her off.

Daniel sensed Muriel's tension, though he couldn't fathom the cause. Couldn't she tell how right this was? He felt so peaceful.

"Thank you," he said. "For helping us."

The old man nodded, rocking his chair back. He seemed content for the moment to sit in silence.

Muriel tensed again, and Daniel squeezed her hand, gently, to reassure her. He knew she had to be wondering what was going on. He should tell her his secret, but he was terrified she would turn away from him. Maybe the old man would know what to do. If only he could find a way to ask without revealing anything.

The old man smiled, as if he knew Daniel's thoughts. "Relax, children. All things are revealed in time."

Revealed. Maybe he could read thoughts. Daniel winced. He should think less.

Muriel settled back in her chair. It was good to see her starting to relax. She'd been through so much today.

He pulled his hand out of hers and ran his fingers up her arm. He rested his hand on her shoulder, and she seemed to draw comfort from it. Her head tilted, her cheek rubbing against his knuckles.

The old man cleared his throat, and their eyes darted back to him, faces flushed with a guilty awareness.

Daniel thought the man was about to say something, instead he tapped his pipe against the side of the fireplace and began to refill it. Muriel leaned in closer, also thinking the old man was about to speak, then sat back when she realized that this was not the case.

After a long silence, the man lit his pipe. The smell of tobacco filled the room.

"A long while I have waited for you two," the old man finally said. "I hope it was worth it."

Daniel hesitated. What could this possibly mean? "I'm afraid I don't understand, sir."

"I know you don't, child. Not yet anyway," said the old man. "It will be quite some time before you truly do. In the meantime, let's have some tea."

He wandered out into the dimness and came back with a tea kettle, which he hung from a hook over the fire. The flames crackled below it, casting his shadow across the circle of light. He turned to face them.

"See my shadow?" he began. "It begins in the light, then is lost in darkness." He slowly made his way back to his chair and sat.

"We are all lost in darkness now," he said. "We started in the light. It's time we found our way back." He puffed on his pipe and then frowned at it because it had now gone out.

Daniel leaned towards him, his hands spread outwards. "Sir, thank you for your help. But I don't know what you want from us."

The old man smiled. "It's not about what I want. You will do everything you are meant to do, whether I wish it or no. I am just the messenger."

"What is your message for us?" Muriel asked.

The old man re-lit his pipe. "I am here to show you the path, that's all," he said. "Should you choose to follow it, the rest is up to you."

"The rest? The rest of what?" asked Daniel.

The old man looked at them wistfully. "I remember a time when I was your age. We all had such dreams back then. All of them are gone now, I am the last."

"I am confused, sir, who are you?" Daniel asked. "I don't even know your name."

The old man puffed on his pipe a while, deep in thought. "Do you believe in magic, child?"

"Magic?" Daniel smiled. "Magic is..." He hesitated. His thoughts wandered back over recent events. Events he wasn't sure he understood. His eyes locked with Muriel's.

"I am the last gatekeeper, son. In olden days, we kept things on the right path by keeping the world in balance. I'm hoping that the two of you, with your unique skills, can put things right again." The old man paused, taking a long draw on his pipe.

"Unique skills?" Daniel asked slowly. He wondered how much the man knew or guessed about him and where he had come from. His thoughts strayed to the contents of his pack. He wondered what skills Muriel might possess that this man considered so valuable.

Muriel shifted in her seat. "I have to tell you something," she said quietly. "I have not been completely honest with you, Daniel."

In the following silence, the tea kettle began to whistle.

Meepo.

Starting items: Stout Shield, Ring of Protection, Tangoes, Iron Branch

Rush BoT, don't be afraid to sell the RoP or SS to get it a bit faster. The SS/RoP allow your main Meepo to tank camps early while Poofing them down.

For a farming build go 1: Poof 2: Nothing 3: Poof + 2nd Meepo

In a lane against melee heroes or heroes without an escape grab an Orb of Venom and go the following: 1: Geostrike 2: Nothing 3: Geostrike + 2nd Meepo. You will have a 32% slow at 2~ mins and be able to right click down any hero that does not have an escape. After your first kill get Boots and then you will be able to kill any hero that crosses the safe threshold almost every time.

This build is especially good for mid. Drop the RoP + Iron branch in mid and go Tangoes, Stout, Orb of Venom. Lv1 Geostrike and OOV means that one hit on a mid hero will do a fair bit of niggling damage.

For early kills micro is important. Chase with one Meepo by running alongside the enemy (but don't attack!) and poof the other Meepo to him. Then right click with both (for the slow) and channel Poof with your other Meepo. Then right click down whoever it was you were chasing. a 0-1-1-1 build is legit for early aggression.
